observations:
Torah #119 (LM2) contains no bechina relationships — neither in the dataset (reference 1119 has zero edges in torahData.js) nor in the source text itself. The teaching uses no bechina language and draws no conceptual equivalences. It is a short aggadic/ethical discourse in which the Rebbe observes the universality of worldly suffering and instructs that the only remedy is to redirect one's toil toward Torah study.

Since the entire teaching's conceptual structure is eitza (cause → effect, problem → remedy) rather than bechina (parallel expressions of the same essential nature), there is no basis for forming any packages — neither from the existing dataset nor from the source text.

The key concepts mentioned in the text (יסורים, עמל, תורה, עולם הזה, עולם הבא, גיהנם) exist in the broader dataset under other Torah references, but within this Torah they are related only by cause-and-effect: suffering exists universally → the only escape is Torah → Torah study transforms worldly toil into Torah toil → one thereby escapes worldly suffering and earns the World to Come. This is a single linear eitza chain, not a web of bechina equivalences from which packages could be constructed.

Conclusion: NO_NEW_PACKAGES. This Torah does not contribute any bechina-based conceptual clusters to the dataset. It stands as a purely ethical/exhortatory teaching.
